name: connect-model-legacy-cleanup
description: What: One-time cleanup of the Main instance: back up the database, then delete every Connect strategy and service configuration that is not this family's. Never deletes an entity. Run connect-model-legacy-cleanup-preview first. Why: A building block of the Connect pack; a test, setup or schedule workload runs it so its steps exist once. When: Never run directly once the pack is tested; its parents run it. Running it alone is safe only when its own Needs are met. Needs: reference values: connect/databases:ProfiseeDatabaseName, connect/instances:ProfiseeInstanceName, connect/machines:ApplicationServerName, connect/machines:ApplicationServerNameFQDN, connect/machines:DatabaseServerName, connect/urls:ConnectBaseUrl. Success: Every step Succeeded or Skipped. If it fails: Run connect-preflight first; then open the first failed step, whose If it fails text names what to check.

globalParameters.KeepStrategies: Strategy Source Data Load|Strategy SQL Server Export|Strategy SQL Server Import|Strategy Profisee To Profisee Export|Strategy Databricks Export|Strategy Databricks Import|Strategy Snowflake Export|Strategy Snowflake Import|Strategy Synapse Export|Strategy Synapse Import
globalParameters.KeepServiceConfigurations: Service Configuration SQL Server Model Source|Service Configuration SQL Server Connect Export|Service Configuration Profisee To Profisee|Service Configuration Databricks|Service Configuration Snowflake|Service Configuration Synapse|Profisee File Repository Service Configuration

globalParametersNotes: The lists are read at run time. KeepStrategies and KeepServiceConfigurations are |-separated names.

inline.description: What: Safety backup of the Main database before anything is deleted. Restore it with connect-database-reset (set BackupFileName) to undo the cleanup. Why: Backs up or restores the database so every run starts from the same known state (BackupDatabase). Success: SQL Server finishes the BackupDatabase of the database with the named file in its default backup folder. If it fails: Check the backup file exists in the SQL Server default backup folder of the database server, the disk has room, and the CrewChief account is sysadmin there.

What: Gateway check: list entities. Accepts ONLY 200 so a wrong address (404) or a wrong key (401) stops the run before anything is created or deleted. Why: Calls the Profisee or TestAuto REST API for this change or check, the same way a client would. Success: The response status is one of the expected codes (200). If it fails: 401 = the API key is not set on that instance yet (run connect-setup) or the secret is wrong; 404 = the record, entity or address is missing; no response = the server in the URL (connect/urls, connect/machines) is down.

What: Delete the legacy Connect strategies and service configurations read from the instance now. Never deletes an entity. Fails listing anything left. Why: Does work no single built-in step does (several calls, waits or checks in one place) and stops at the first problem. Success: The script finishes without an error; its output lines say what it did. If it fails: Read the last output line and the error text: the script names the value, server or record it could not handle.

inputs.name: ProfiseeVersionCode
inputs.description: TestAuto version code (data.tProfiseeVersion) the runs are recorded under; the automation tags, run profile codes and backup names carry it. Passed by the test that runs this one (connect/environment:ProfiseeVersionCode, or the lane's version).
